title: Bounded integer histogram
instructions:
Implement a counter for integer measurements with fixed-width bins.

## Files
- `histogram.py`: implement `BoundedHistogram`.

Public API (all methods are instance methods):
- `BoundedHistogram(low: int, high: int, width: int)`: inclusive bounds;
  require low <= high and width > 0, otherwise raise ValueError. Bounds and
  width must be integers other than bool, otherwise raise TypeError.
- `add(value: int, count: int = 1) -> None`: value and count must be integers
  other than bool (TypeError otherwise); count must be nonnegative (ValueError).
  A value outside the inclusive bounds raises ValueError even for count=0.
  Add count occurrences to the bin containing value. Validation failures
  leave all counts unchanged.
- `count(value: int) -> int`: return the total count of the BIN containing
  value, not just occurrences of that exact value. Apply the same type and
  range validation as add's value.
- `bins() -> list[tuple[int, int, int]]`: return (start, end, count) for every
  bin in increasing order, including empty bins. Bin ends are inclusive and
  the last end is clipped to high. Return a fresh list on every call.
- `reset() -> None`: zero all counts while retaining the bin configuration.

Bins start at low and every width thereafter. For example bounds -2..4 and
width 3 produce [-2..0], [1..3], [4..4]. Use only the standard library.
